prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce proximity between a target protein and the ubiquitin-proteasome system so that the cell removes the protein rather than merely inhibiting it

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B026 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After round 1 the case rests on three things I think are now agreed by all eight members. First, the mechanism is quantitative and independently reproduced: ternary-complex formation, cooperativity and degradation kinetics are measured, not assumed, and no one has questioned them. Second, it is new in the sense I use the word: a designable chemical reaction in which a small molecule directs the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery, which turns inhibition into removal and reaches targets that occupancy-driven drugs could not. Third, it has already had consequences that do not depend on an approved PROTAC: the cereblon mechanism explains the lenalidomide-class glues that are in clinical use, so the induced-proximity principle is validated in patients. In answer to the chair's first question, my standard is established mechanism, independent replication and demonstrated consequences, not approval of a particular drug class. For the citation I would anchor it on induced proximity as one principle, with Crews and Deshaies for the design concept and Handa for the discovery that cereblon is the thalidomide target, which lets one citation cover both glues and PROTACs. In chemical terms the citation says that a small molecule can be designed to bring two proteins together so that one is ubiquitinated and destroyed.
statement.case_against: The objections I take most seriously are unchanged and I do not think round 1 removed them. No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, and I have not verified clinical status, so the committee is partly betting on trajectory. The three-person limit omits Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the field rationally designable, as well as Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito. Somfai's point that much of the chemistry is linker and ligand design on known E3 ligands is fair, and the cereblon story is partly pharmacology. If the committee judged that the citation depends on PROTAC drugs rather than on the principle, I would agree it is premature. Finally, a three-name prize for a field with eight credible names will be criticised whatever we do, so the omissions must be stated openly as a consequence of the three-person rule and not as a judgement on merit.

responses.point: Peter now prefers B026 but says the PROTAC and glue arms are partly distinct achievements, and that Ciulli's role must be checked before we settle on Crews, Deshaies and Handa.
responses.response: I agree that the two arms are distinct historically but not mechanistically: both bring a target to an E3 ligase and rely on ternary-complex formation, which is the physical description Peter himself gave. That is why I want the citation worded as induced proximity and not as PROTAC drugs. On Ciulli, I have thought about it again. His work is a decisive refinement that made the principle designable, but it follows the proof of concept and the cereblon discovery, and a prize for the principle is best anchored on what was shown first and on what was found in nature. I therefore keep Deshaies and Handa, and I say plainly that this is a priority judgement under a three-person limit. I also accept Peter's earlier point that PROTAC approval is pending and I have stopped calling it irrelevant: it is not required for the principle, but it would strengthen the case for timing.

responses.point: Peter Somfai says the chemistry in B026 is mostly linker and ligand design on known E3 ligands, that much of the achievement is biology and pharmacology, and that he could back B026 if the maturity argument is stated honestly.
responses.response: I accept the request to state maturity honestly: the committee would be rewarding a principle with approved glue drugs and many late-stage PROTACs, not an approved PROTAC. On the chemistry, I disagree in part. Designing a molecule so that it forms a productive and cooperative ternary complex is a physical-organic problem, not only a matter of attaching a linker, and the cereblon result shows a small molecule reshaping a protein surface to create a new binding interface, which is molecular recognition in a strict sense. I do not claim this is as clean a synthetic invention as C-N coupling, which I agree is a mature and well-attributed achievement. My difficulty with B060 is the one he and Zou record: it extends the 2010 palladium prize. Because Somfai lists B026 as his alternative, I would ask whether a citation worded in terms of induced proximity and ternary-complex design would be enough for him to support it in a final configuration.

responses.point: Heiner, our chair, would keep Handa over Ciulli, treats the cereblon result as what lets one citation cover glues, and now treats sequencing (B067) as a fall-back.
responses.response: We agree, and I agree with his test of what was discovered and when. Handa and Ito explained why thalidomide-type drugs act, which is a discovery about nature, while Ciulli's work refined a principle that already existed. I would add one point on Ito: Handa and Ito shared that work, and I would not call Handa alone the discoverer, so the omission of Ito needs the same open statement as that of Ciulli. On B067, the chair's question is whether the Solexa chemistry is separable from the 454 and Mayer lineages. I cannot answer that from the material I am allowed to see, and that is why I now list it as my second alternative and not a preferred part. I agree its merit is not in question; the doubts are about attribution and about its closeness to Physiology or Medicine.

responses.point: Emma holds that condensates meet the game-changer criterion because they changed how a discipline asks where molecules are organised, and that Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen are a cleaner attribution core than my B026 trio.
responses.response: I accept that condensates changed how biologists think, and I do not dismiss the physical-chemical argument. But my criterion is demonstrated consequences established by quantitative evidence, and Emma herself concedes in her case against that in vivo condensates are not always shown to be equilibrium phase-separated systems and that functional consequences are demonstrated for fewer cases than the concept suggests. She did not answer my earlier question about which in-cell measurements she regards as firm. I also do not agree that the attribution of B031 is cleaner: leaving out Pappu and Mittag removes the sticker-and-spacer framework that provides the quantitative content, and for B026 the omissions are of refinements of an established mechanism. I therefore remain unable to support B031 at this time, and I would regard it as a strong candidate in a later year.

responses.point: Andrei would credit base editing to David R. Liu alone, and sees Komor and Gaudelli as laboratory members.
responses.response: I have moved toward his view. In round 1 I defended Komor and Gaudelli as separate inventors, but with the three-person limit and the Target-AID work of Nishida and Kondo making the credit contestable, a Liu-only configuration is the most defensible form of B038 and I would support it if B026 does not carry. I still read the evolution of a deaminase to act on DNA as chemistry, but I accept that the field is young and follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, which is why B038 is only an alternative.

uncertainties: I have not verified clinical status for degraders or approved lenalidomide-class glues and am relying on recollection and on what colleagues have said.
Whether the omission of Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito can be defended without a reader seeing the cut as arbitrary, and whether Ito should be paired with Handa in a final configuration.
Whether Peter Somfai, Zou and Emma Sparr will support B026 in a final configuration, and under what condition.
Whether the committee reads the chemistry in B026 as sufficient, or as primarily pharmacology; I cannot settle this from the material I am allowed to read.
Whether B067 can be separated from the 454, Mayer and Ju lineages; I have no basis to resolve it.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I disclose no tie to any credited name on the shortlist. My connections are Arieh Warshel (empirical valence bond collaboration), the Uppsala structural biology and ribosome community, and my committee colleagues, including Peter Brzezinski. None of these appear among the credited names for B026, B038 or B067. My field of biomolecular simulation is close to ternary-complex modelling, which could bias me toward B026, and I note that for the record.
